Learn More FAQ's How does CNC machining and 3D printing affect the surface quality of products? CNC machining typically provides a high surface quality with a smooth, fine surface texture. However, the surface quality of 3D printing is usually rough, and subsequent processing is required to achieve a better surface finish. However, with the development of 3D printing technology, some advanced 3D printing methods are also able to provide higher quality surfaces, but usually require additional processing steps. How is the quality control of CNC machining and 3D printing in manufacturing? Both CNC machining and 3D printing require quality control to ensure products meet specifications. In CNC machining, common quality control methods include dimensional inspection using precision measuring tools, surface quality assessment, and functional testing. For 3D printing, quality control includes checking printing parameters, material quality, and print quality, as well as conducting post-processing and testing. How does PCBWay ensure high-quality manufacturing? Equipment Maintenance and Calibration: Regular maintenance and calibration of machine tool equipment is fundamental to ensuring high-quality manufacturing. Maintain the accuracy and performance of equipment, including regular inspection and replacement of tools, checking the accuracy of sensors and measuring instruments, etc. Appropriate process planning: formulate appropriate process planning, including reasonable cutting parameters, tool selection and machining path planning. Ensuring that each process is carefully planned and optimized to achieve the required precision and surface quality requirements. Quality Control Measures: Establish strict quality control measures, including the use of advanced measuring instruments for dimensional inspection and surface quality assessment. Carry out process monitoring and statistical process control to discover and correct potential quality problems in time. Material selection and inspection: Select high-quality raw materials that meet the requirements, and conduct incoming inspection to ensure their quality meets the specifications. Proper material selection is critical to the quality and performance of the final product. Training and skills: Provide necessary training and skill improvement for operators to ensure that they have the correct processing knowledge and technical capabilities, and can accurately operate machine tools and implement process requirements. Continuous improvement: regularly evaluate and analyze the production process, look for opportunities for improvement, and take appropriate measures to improve production efficiency and product quality. Drive continuous improvement with advanced technologies and tools, such as data analytics and automated systems. What services can PCBWay provide you? We offer rapid prototyping, small-scale and large-scale batch manufacturing with CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal, injection molding, vacuum casting and etc. Our factories are ISO-9001 certified, instant online quotation and lead time from 3 days. How to carry out the quality control of CNC machining in manufacturing? Quality control in CNC machining during production manufacturing is crucial to ensure that products meet specifications and requirements. The process involves various steps, including design validation, material inspection, setting appropriate machining parameters, validating CNC programs, conducting first piece inspections, monitoring processes, performing periodic and final inspections, checking surface quality, and maintaining records for traceability. These methods collectively aim to guarantee dimensional accuracy, surface finish, and functionality of the final product. By implementing effective quality control measures, CNC machining ensures consistent and reliable results, meeting the highest standards of quality in various industries. Why are there oil stains on the surface of black resin parts? Resin parts are 3D printed using SLA technology. After printing is complete, remove the supports and sand them. After the product is polished, the surface turns a little white, and then we spray it with a layer of transparent protective oil. The oil is non-toxic and harmless. After you receive it, you can wipe it clean with cotton cloth or wash it with water. Why do 3D printing orders often have EQ regarding wall thickness? The wall thickness directly determines the strength of the printed object, and also determines whether the model can be printed. Once the model is printed, it also goes through support removal, grinding and sandblasting, which determine the minimum wall thickness for different materials. The model is printable only when the wall thickness meets the minimum requirement. However, many 3D printed designs do not meet the standard wall thickness requirements. At this time, there is a risk of damage or even failure in the printing. Another question that everyone is more concerned about is why the wall thickness issue is not pointed out at the beginning of the order review? The reason is that our 3D printing review is based on the automatic quotation of the pricing system, and the system cannot automatically identify some wall thickness issues. Of course, we are also actively developing a more accurate quotation system to ensure the accuracy of quotations while ensuring their timeliness. Anyway, we recommend choosing the following 2 options when placing an order. *Customer knows about the thin walls designed do not meet the wall thickness standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. *Customer knows about the threads designed do not meet the thread printing standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. Why are the CNC or 3D printing parts I receive from different batches different? This problem is common. Since most of our products are prototype, we cannot achieve consistent surface finishes just like batch production. For products without surface treatment, different equipment, different operators, different tools, etc. will lead to differences in the processed surface. For products with surface treatment, due to the particularity and scarcity of the surface finish process, different batches of orders cannot be guaranteed to have the same finish. For example: Aluminum anodized color, there will be color difference more or less with each time, even though you choose the same opition of color. If you need the totally same surface finish of batch products and samples, it is recommended to keep 1-2 samples at PCBWay, and then we can mass-produce the specified products according to the samples. Learn More FAQ's How does CNC machining and 3D printing affect the surface quality of products? CNC machining typically provides a high surface quality with a smooth, fine surface texture. However, the surface quality of 3D printing is usually rough, and subsequent processing is required to achieve a better surface finish. However, with the development of 3D printing technology, some advanced 3D printing methods are also able to provide higher quality surfaces, but usually require additional processing steps. How is the quality control of CNC machining and 3D printing in manufacturing? Both CNC machining and 3D printing require quality control to ensure products meet specifications. In CNC machining, common quality control methods include dimensional inspection using precision measuring tools, surface quality assessment, and functional testing. For 3D printing, quality control includes checking printing parameters, material quality, and print quality, as well as conducting post-processing and testing. How does PCBWay ensure high-quality manufacturing? Equipment Maintenance and Calibration: Regular maintenance and calibration of machine tool equipment is fundamental to ensuring high-quality manufacturing. Maintain the accuracy and performance of equipment, including regular inspection and replacement of tools, checking the accuracy of sensors and measuring instruments, etc. Appropriate process planning: formulate appropriate process planning, including reasonable cutting parameters, tool selection and machining path planning. Ensuring that each process is carefully planned and optimized to achieve the required precision and surface quality requirements. Quality Control Measures: Establish strict quality control measures, including the use of advanced measuring instruments for dimensional inspection and surface quality assessment. Carry out process monitoring and statistical process control to discover and correct potential quality problems in time. Material selection and inspection: Select high-quality raw materials that meet the requirements, and conduct incoming inspection to ensure their quality meets the specifications. Proper material selection is critical to the quality and performance of the final product. Training and skills: Provide necessary training and skill improvement for operators to ensure that they have the correct processing knowledge and technical capabilities, and can accurately operate machine tools and implement process requirements. Continuous improvement: regularly evaluate and analyze the production process, look for opportunities for improvement, and take appropriate measures to improve production efficiency and product quality. Drive continuous improvement with advanced technologies and tools, such as data analytics and automated systems. What services can PCBWay provide you? We offer rapid prototyping, small-scale and large-scale batch manufacturing with CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal, injection molding, vacuum casting and etc. Our factories are ISO-9001 certified, instant online quotation and lead time from 3 days. How to carry out the quality control of CNC machining in manufacturing? Quality control in CNC machining during production manufacturing is crucial to ensure that products meet specifications and requirements. The process involves various steps, including design validation, material inspection, setting appropriate machining parameters, validating CNC programs, conducting first piece inspections, monitoring processes, performing periodic and final inspections, checking surface quality, and maintaining records for traceability. These methods collectively aim to guarantee dimensional accuracy, surface finish, and functionality of the final product. By implementing effective quality control measures, CNC machining ensures consistent and reliable results, meeting the highest standards of quality in various industries. Why are there oil stains on the surface of black resin parts? Resin parts are 3D printed using SLA technology. After printing is complete, remove the supports and sand them. After the product is polished, the surface turns a little white, and then we spray it with a layer of transparent protective oil. The oil is non-toxic and harmless. After you receive it, you can wipe it clean with cotton cloth or wash it with water. Why do 3D printing orders often have EQ regarding wall thickness? The wall thickness directly determines the strength of the printed object, and also determines whether the model can be printed. Once the model is printed, it also goes through support removal, grinding and sandblasting, which determine the minimum wall thickness for different materials. The model is printable only when the wall thickness meets the minimum requirement. However, many 3D printed designs do not meet the standard wall thickness requirements. At this time, there is a risk of damage or even failure in the printing. Another question that everyone is more concerned about is why the wall thickness issue is not pointed out at the beginning of the order review? The reason is that our 3D printing review is based on the automatic quotation of the pricing system, and the system cannot automatically identify some wall thickness issues. Of course, we are also actively developing a more accurate quotation system to ensure the accuracy of quotations while ensuring their timeliness. Anyway, we recommend choosing the following 2 options when placing an order. *Customer knows about the thin walls designed do not meet the wall thickness standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. *Customer knows about the threads designed do not meet the thread printing standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. Why are the CNC or 3D printing parts I receive from different batches different? This problem is common. Since most of our products are prototype, we cannot achieve consistent surface finishes just like batch production. For products without surface treatment, different equipment, different operators, different tools, etc. will lead to differences in the processed surface. For products with surface treatment, due to the particularity and scarcity of the surface finish process, different batches of orders cannot be guaranteed to have the same finish. For example: Aluminum anodized color, there will be color difference more or less with each time, even though you choose the same opition of color. If you need the totally same surface finish of batch products and samples, it is recommended to keep 1-2 samples at PCBWay, and then we can mass-produce the specified products according to the samples. However, the surface quality of 3D printing is usually rough, and subsequent processing is required to achieve a better surface finish. However, with the development of 3D printing technology, some advanced 3D printing methods are also able to provide higher quality surfaces, but usually require additional processing steps. How is the quality control of CNC machining and 3D printing in manufacturing? Both CNC machining and 3D printing require quality control to ensure products meet specifications. In CNC machining, common quality control methods include dimensional inspection using precision measuring tools, surface quality assessment, and functional testing. For 3D printing, quality control includes checking printing parameters, material quality, and print quality, as well as conducting post-processing and testing. How does PCBWay ensure high-quality manufacturing? Equipment Maintenance and Calibration: Regular maintenance and calibration of machine tool equipment is fundamental to ensuring high-quality manufacturing. Maintain the accuracy and performance of equipment, including regular inspection and replacement of tools, checking the accuracy of sensors and measuring instruments, etc. Appropriate process planning: formulate appropriate process planning, including reasonable cutting parameters, tool selection and machining path planning. Ensuring that each process is carefully planned and optimized to achieve the required precision and surface quality requirements. Quality Control Measures: Establish strict quality control measures, including the use of advanced measuring instruments for dimensional inspection and surface quality assessment. Carry out process monitoring and statistical process control to discover and correct potential quality problems in time. Material selection and inspection: Select high-quality raw materials that meet the requirements, and conduct incoming inspection to ensure their quality meets the specifications. Proper material selection is critical to the quality and performance of the final product. Training and skills: Provide necessary training and skill improvement for operators to ensure that they have the correct processing knowledge and technical capabilities, and can accurately operate machine tools and implement process requirements. Continuous improvement: regularly evaluate and analyze the production process, look for opportunities for improvement, and take appropriate measures to improve production efficiency and product quality. Drive continuous improvement with advanced technologies and tools, such as data analytics and automated systems. What services can PCBWay provide you? We offer rapid prototyping, small-scale and large-scale batch manufacturing with CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal, injection molding, vacuum casting and etc. Our factories are ISO-9001 certified, instant online quotation and lead time from 3 days. How to carry out the quality control of CNC machining in manufacturing? Quality control in CNC machining during production manufacturing is crucial to ensure that products meet specifications and requirements. The process involves various steps, including design validation, material inspection, setting appropriate machining parameters, validating CNC programs, conducting first piece inspections, monitoring processes, performing periodic and final inspections, checking surface quality, and maintaining records for traceability. These methods collectively aim to guarantee dimensional accuracy, surface finish, and functionality of the final product. By implementing effective quality control measures, CNC machining ensures consistent and reliable results, meeting the highest standards of quality in various industries. Why are there oil stains on the surface of black resin parts? Resin parts are 3D printed using SLA technology. After printing is complete, remove the supports and sand them. After the product is polished, the surface turns a little white, and then we spray it with a layer of transparent protective oil. The oil is non-toxic and harmless. After you receive it, you can wipe it clean with cotton cloth or wash it with water. Why do 3D printing orders often have EQ regarding wall thickness? The wall thickness directly determines the strength of the printed object, and also determines whether the model can be printed. Once the model is printed, it also goes through support removal, grinding and sandblasting, which determine the minimum wall thickness for different materials. The model is printable only when the wall thickness meets the minimum requirement. However, many 3D printed designs do not meet the standard wall thickness requirements. At this time, there is a risk of damage or even failure in the printing. Another question that everyone is more concerned about is why the wall thickness issue is not pointed out at the beginning of the order review? The reason is that our 3D printing review is based on the automatic quotation of the pricing system, and the system cannot automatically identify some wall thickness issues. Of course, we are also actively developing a more accurate quotation system to ensure the accuracy of quotations while ensuring their timeliness. Anyway, we recommend choosing the following 2 options when placing an order. *Customer knows about the thin walls designed do not meet the wall thickness standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. *Customer knows about the threads designed do not meet the thread printing standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. Why are the CNC or 3D printing parts I receive from different batches different? This problem is common. Since most of our products are prototype, we cannot achieve consistent surface finishes just like batch production. For products without surface treatment, different equipment, different operators, different tools, etc. will lead to differences in the processed surface. For products with surface treatment, due to the particularity and scarcity of the surface finish process, different batches of orders cannot be guaranteed to have the same finish. For example: Aluminum anodized color, there will be color difference more or less with each time, even though you choose the same opition of color. If you need the totally same surface finish of batch products and samples, it is recommended to keep 1-2 samples at PCBWay, and then we can mass-produce the specified products according to the samples. Learn More FAQ's How does CNC machining and 3D printing affect the surface quality of products? CNC machining typically provides a high surface quality with a smooth, fine surface texture. However, the surface quality of 3D printing is usually rough, and subsequent processing is required to achieve a better surface finish. However, with the development of 3D printing technology, some advanced 3D printing methods are also able to provide higher quality surfaces, but usually require additional processing steps. How is the quality control of CNC machining and 3D printing in manufacturing? Both CNC machining and 3D printing require quality control to ensure products meet specifications. In CNC machining, common quality control methods include dimensional inspection using precision measuring tools, surface quality assessment, and functional testing. For 3D printing, quality control includes checking printing parameters, material quality, and print quality, as well as conducting post-processing and testing. How does PCBWay ensure high-quality manufacturing? Equipment Maintenance and Calibration: Regular maintenance and calibration of machine tool equipment is fundamental to ensuring high-quality manufacturing. Maintain the accuracy and performance of equipment, including regular inspection and replacement of tools, checking the accuracy of sensors and measuring instruments, etc. Appropriate process planning: formulate appropriate process planning, including reasonable cutting parameters, tool selection and machining path planning. Ensuring that each process is carefully planned and optimized to achieve the required precision and surface quality requirements. Quality Control Measures: Establish strict quality control measures, including the use of advanced measuring instruments for dimensional inspection and surface quality assessment. Carry out process monitoring and statistical process control to discover and correct potential quality problems in time. Material selection and inspection: Select high-quality raw materials that meet the requirements, and conduct incoming inspection to ensure their quality meets the specifications. Proper material selection is critical to the quality and performance of the final product. Training and skills: Provide necessary training and skill improvement for operators to ensure that they have the correct processing knowledge and technical capabilities, and can accurately operate machine tools and implement process requirements. Continuous improvement: regularly evaluate and analyze the production process, look for opportunities for improvement, and take appropriate measures to improve production efficiency and product quality. Drive continuous improvement with advanced technologies and tools, such as data analytics and automated systems. What services can PCBWay provide you? We offer rapid prototyping, small-scale and large-scale batch manufacturing with CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal, injection molding, vacuum casting and etc. Our factories are ISO-9001 certified, instant online quotation and lead time from 3 days. How to carry out the quality control of CNC machining in manufacturing? Quality control in CNC machining during production manufacturing is crucial to ensure that products meet specifications and requirements. The process involves various steps, including design validation, material inspection, setting appropriate machining parameters, validating CNC programs, conducting first piece inspections, monitoring processes, performing periodic and final inspections, checking surface quality, and maintaining records for traceability. These methods collectively aim to guarantee dimensional accuracy, surface finish, and functionality of the final product. By implementing effective quality control measures, CNC machining ensures consistent and reliable results, meeting the highest standards of quality in various industries. Why are there oil stains on the surface of black resin parts? Resin parts are 3D printed using SLA technology. After printing is complete, remove the supports and sand them. After the product is polished, the surface turns a little white, and then we spray it with a layer of transparent protective oil. The oil is non-toxic and harmless. After you receive it, you can wipe it clean with cotton cloth or wash it with water. Why do 3D printing orders often have EQ regarding wall thickness? The wall thickness directly determines the strength of the printed object, and also determines whether the model can be printed. Once the model is printed, it also goes through support removal, grinding and sandblasting, which determine the minimum wall thickness for different materials. The model is printable only when the wall thickness meets the minimum requirement. However, many 3D printed designs do not meet the standard wall thickness requirements. At this time, there is a risk of damage or even failure in the printing. Another question that everyone is more concerned about is why the wall thickness issue is not pointed out at the beginning of the order review? The reason is that our 3D printing review is based on the automatic quotation of the pricing system, and the system cannot automatically identify some wall thickness issues. Of course, we are also actively developing a more accurate quotation system to ensure the accuracy of quotations while ensuring their timeliness. Anyway, we recommend choosing the following 2 options when placing an order. *Customer knows about the thin walls designed do not meet the wall thickness standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. *Customer knows about the threads designed do not meet the thread printing standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. Why are the CNC or 3D printing parts I receive from different batches different? This problem is common. Since most of our products are prototype, we cannot achieve consistent surface finishes just like batch production. For products without surface treatment, different equipment, different operators, different tools, etc. will lead to differences in the processed surface. For products with surface treatment, due to the particularity and scarcity of the surface finish process, different batches of orders cannot be guaranteed to have the same finish. For example: Aluminum anodized color, there will be color difference more or less with each time, even though you choose the same opition of color. If you need the totally same surface finish of batch products and samples, it is recommended to keep 1-2 samples at PCBWay, and then we can mass-produce the specified products according to the samples. Learn More FAQ's How does CNC machining and 3D printing affect the surface quality of products? CNC machining typically provides a high surface quality with a smooth, fine surface texture. However, the surface quality of 3D printing is usually rough, and subsequent processing is required to achieve a better surface finish. However, with the development of 3D printing technology, some advanced 3D printing methods are also able to provide higher quality surfaces, but usually require additional processing steps. How is the quality control of CNC machining and 3D printing in manufacturing? Both CNC machining and 3D printing require quality control to ensure products meet specifications. In CNC machining, common quality control methods include dimensional inspection using precision measuring tools, surface quality assessment, and functional testing. For 3D printing, quality control includes checking printing parameters, material quality, and print quality, as well as conducting post-processing and testing. How does PCBWay ensure high-quality manufacturing? Equipment Maintenance and Calibration: Regular maintenance and calibration of machine tool equipment is fundamental to ensuring high-quality manufacturing. Maintain the accuracy and performance of equipment, including regular inspection and replacement of tools, checking the accuracy of sensors and measuring instruments, etc. Appropriate process planning: formulate appropriate process planning, including reasonable cutting parameters, tool selection and machining path planning. Ensuring that each process is carefully planned and optimized to achieve the required precision and surface quality requirements. Quality Control Measures: Establish strict quality control measures, including the use of advanced measuring instruments for dimensional inspection and surface quality assessment. Carry out process monitoring and statistical process control to discover and correct potential quality problems in time. Material selection and inspection: Select high-quality raw materials that meet the requirements, and conduct incoming inspection to ensure their quality meets the specifications. Proper material selection is critical to the quality and performance of the final product. Training and skills: Provide necessary training and skill improvement for operators to ensure that they have the correct processing knowledge and technical capabilities, and can accurately operate machine tools and implement process requirements. Continuous improvement: regularly evaluate and analyze the production process, look for opportunities for improvement, and take appropriate measures to improve production efficiency and product quality. Drive continuous improvement with advanced technologies and tools, such as data analytics and automated systems. What services can PCBWay provide you? We offer rapid prototyping, small-scale and large-scale batch manufacturing with CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal, injection molding, vacuum casting and etc. Our factories are ISO-9001 certified, instant online quotation and lead time from 3 days. How to carry out the quality control of CNC machining in manufacturing? Quality control in CNC machining during production manufacturing is crucial to ensure that products meet specifications and requirements. The process involves various steps, including design validation, material inspection, setting appropriate machining parameters, validating CNC programs, conducting first piece inspections, monitoring processes, performing periodic and final inspections, checking surface quality, and maintaining records for traceability. These methods collectively aim to guarantee dimensional accuracy, surface finish, and functionality of the final product. By implementing effective quality control measures, CNC machining ensures consistent and reliable results, meeting the highest standards of quality in various industries. Why are there oil stains on the surface of black resin parts? Resin parts are 3D printed using SLA technology. After printing is complete, remove the supports and sand them. After the product is polished, the surface turns a little white, and then we spray it with a layer of transparent protective oil. The oil is non-toxic and harmless. After you receive it, you can wipe it clean with cotton cloth or wash it with water. Why do 3D printing orders often have EQ regarding wall thickness? The wall thickness directly determines the strength of the printed object, and also determines whether the model can be printed. Once the model is printed, it also goes through support removal, grinding and sandblasting, which determine the minimum wall thickness for different materials. The model is printable only when the wall thickness meets the minimum requirement. However, many 3D printed designs do not meet the standard wall thickness requirements. At this time, there is a risk of damage or even failure in the printing. Another question that everyone is more concerned about is why the wall thickness issue is not pointed out at the beginning of the order review? The reason is that our 3D printing review is based on the automatic quotation of the pricing system, and the system cannot automatically identify some wall thickness issues. Of course, we are also actively developing a more accurate quotation system to ensure the accuracy of quotations while ensuring their timeliness. Anyway, we recommend choosing the following 2 options when placing an order. *Customer knows about the thin walls designed do not meet the wall thickness standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. *Customer knows about the threads designed do not meet the thread printing standard, but needs to print as-is and take all risks. Why are the CNC or 3D printing parts I receive from different batches different? This problem is common. Since most of our products are prototype, we cannot achieve consistent surface finishes just like batch production. For products without surface treatment, different equipment, different operators, different tools, etc. will lead to differences in the processed surface. For products with surface treatment, due to the particularity and scarcity of the surface finish process, different batches of orders cannot be guaranteed to have the same finish. For example: Aluminum anodized color, there will be color difference more or less with each time, even though you choose the same opition of color. If you need the totally same surface finish of batch products and samples, it is recommended to keep 1-2 samples at PCBWay, and then we can mass-produce the specified products according to the samples. events.summary: 板块文案更新：Thread Milling vs. Tapping: What’s the Difference and When to Use Each?
events.before: Thread Milling vs. Tapping: What’s the Difference and When to Use Each? Published Jul 29, 2025, updated Jul 28, 2025 5 min Threading a hole sounds simple, until you’re deciding between thread milling and tapping . Both methods are staples in CNC machining and manual operations, but they serve different purposes, machines, and tolerances. Whether you're threading aluminum, stainless steel, or titanium, choosing the wrong method can mean broken tools, scrapped parts, or wasted hours. Let’s break down the real differences between thread milling vs tapping , when to use one over the other, and how to choose the right tool for your part. What is Tapping? Tapping is the traditional method of creating internal threads by driving a tap, a hardened cutting tool, into a pre-drilled hole. It’s fast, easy to set up, and widely used in manual and CNC operations. There are three common types of taps: ● Hand taps – used manually with a T-handle ● Spiral point taps – best for through holes ● Spiral flute taps – best for blind holes Taps are typically specific to one thread size and pitch, which makes them convenient but rigid in flexibility. events.summary: 板块文案更新：4. Process Limitations & Design Considerations
events.before: 4. Process Limitations & Design Considerations Manufacturing Note: While electro-discharge processing solves difficult geometry problems, design engineers must account for material conductivity limits, lower volumetric removal rates, and thermal surface alterations. Material Restrictions: Process applies exclusively to electrically conductive materials; polymers, ceramics, and glass cannot be eroded. Slower Material Removal Rate (MRR): Compared to heavy CNC milling or turning, removal rates are lower, making it ideal for finishing and specialized features rather than rough bulk removal. Higher Operational Costs: Equipment investments, electrode wear, dielectric management, and higher energy consumption make it best suited for high-value components. Recast Layer & Heat-Affected Zone (HAZ): Thermal erosion creates a micro-thin recast layer on the cut surface, which may require secondary polishing for critical fatigue-rated parts. Electrode Tool Wear: Unlike non-contact ideal states, spark erosion gradually degrades the electrode shape, requiring compensation in cnc edm sinker routines.

events.summary: 板块文案更新：2. How the Output Capacitor Affects LDO Loop Stability
events.before: 2. How the Output Capacitor Affects LDO Loop Stability In a simplified small-signal model, the output capacitor and the equivalent output load impedance form an output pole, whose frequency is expressed as: f pole = 1 / (2 × π × R OUT × C OUT ) Assuming an output equivalent resistance of 0.1 Ω: a 10µF capacitor creates an output pole at approximately 159 kHz, whereas increasing the capacitor to 100µF shifts the pole down to roughly 15.9 kHz. This calculation illustrates how capacitance influences pole placement; in actual practice, loop poles are also shaped by the pass element, error amplifier, feedback network, and internal compensation circuits. Within any robust power supply design, the output capacitor and its equivalent series resistance (ESR) alter the location of output poles and zeros, dictating crossover frequency and phase margin. As capacitance increases, the output pole moves to lower frequencies, potentially reducing loop crossover frequency or degrading phase margin. Whether this induces oscillation depends on internal compensation, capacitor ESR, load conditions, and phase margin reserves.

In this session, we’ll explore how DMLS enables intricate geometries, internal channels and features, thin walls, tight spaces, and consolidated assemblies that can improve device performance and reduce design constraints. We’ll also discuss how engineers can balance complex, performance-driven designs with manufacturability, and where secondary machining may complement additive manufacturing to achieve critical features and tolerances. Whether you’re developing early prototypes or refining components for testing, this webinar will highlight where DMLS can create value in medical device development. Register Now

events.summary: 板块文案更新：A Xometry Solution: Flexibility, Reliability, Cost-Savings, and Freedom to Focus
events.before: A Xometry Solution: Flexibility, Reliability, Cost-Savings, and Freedom to Focus Flexible Supply Chain Xometry manufactures parts for Asylon as the startup needs them, allowing the growing company to quickly adapt to changes in demand and maintain high confidence in the saleability of existing units. Siu describes Asylon’s product development process as “creating aerospace-quality designs with startup agility.” A Reliable, High-Quality Drone Product Xometry manufactured production-grade sheet metal parts for Asylon’s drone station. The station is large in size, measuring approximately 72" wide, 72” long, and 36” tall. (This size accounts for larger sized drones measuring up to 48” from wingtip to wingtip.) Since the sheet metal parts Siu designed are very large, other manufacturers were unable to provide an anodize finish. A vast partner network allowed Xometry to source a suitable machine shop for the job, thereby ensuring DroneHome’s durability against precipitation-based corrosion.
